title: Affine open supported model existence
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with derived categories of module sheaves and of its localized open sites [def-pc-derived-category], and let $Eprime$ have quasi-coherent cohomology. For an affine open $U$ and integer $k$, put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$, and let $R$ be derived over-site restriction. With a derived category of $A$-modules fixed, let $F:D(A)\to D(\mathcal O_X\text{ over }U)$ have a natural isomorphism $F\circ Q\cong Q\circ\operatorname{affinePerfectSheafification}_*$ on complexes [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model]. Then there is $M\in D(A)$ with $F(M)\cong R(Eprime[k])$. No scalar, support, boundedness or perfectness assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 08EJ, affine support paragraph; Tag 06Z0 exact associated sheaf

proof.text: The homology shift isomorphism identifies H^n(Eprime[k]) with H^(k+n)(Eprime), hence it is quasi-coherent. Construct the actual sheaf equivalence t from restriction along isoSpec and Modules.overEquiv.inverse, and derive its two functors by Functor.mapDerivedCategory. Derive its counit by the composition, natural-isomorphism and identity comparisons. Put K = D(overFunctor followed by t.inverse)(Eprime[k]). The composite overFunctor followed by t.inverse is naturally isomorphic to restriction along isoSpec.inv followed by the open immersion. Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso identify each homology sheaf of K with this restriction of the shifted homology. Mathlib Modules.isQuasicoherent_restrictFunctor and invariance under isomorphism show that K belongs to D_QCoh(Spec A).

Apply [new-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence-core] in the standard derived category of sheaf modules on Spec A and the given derived category of A-modules. Take M = e.inverse(K). Whisker its termwise tilde comparison by D(t.functor). The exact-functor factorization and mapHomologicalComplexCompIso identify this composite after Q with Q of the explicit affinePerfectSheafification complex [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model]. The normalization on shifts in the larger affine equivalence theorem is not needed.

Compose hF with the inverse of the preceding comparison to obtain Q followed by F isomorphic to Q followed by G, where G is affine derived tilde followed by D(t.functor). The given module localization is pinned explicitly, with identity Lifting isomorphisms for its composites with F and G. Localization.liftNatIso descends the comparison to F isomorphic to G. Evaluate at M, apply D(t.functor) to the affine equivalence counit at K, and compose with the counit of D(t). This yields F(M) isomorphic to the required over-site restriction of Eprime[k]. Every chosen object is given by an explicit functor or an equivalence inverse. No support or boundedness is used, and the same construction applies when U is empty.

proof_origin.note: Lean proof using the existing affine core equivalence, explicit canonical chart transport, exact-functor homology comparisons and localization uniqueness; no new holes.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_open_supported_model_exists
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E' : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (k : ℤ)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (ModuleCat.{u} (X.sheaf.obj.obj (op U)))]
    (F : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (X.sheaf.obj.obj (op U))) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)))
    (hF : Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ F ≅
      (affinePerfectSheafification X U hU).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q)) :
    ∃ M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (X.sheaf.obj.obj (op U))),
      Nonempty (F.obj M ≅
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (E'.obj⟦k⟧))
